questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x}{{y}^{2}}, & \,0<x<y,\,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(\frac{1}{4}<X<\frac{1}{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{5}{8}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(X\in A\,|\,Y=y)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\frac{1}{4}<X<\frac{1}{2}\,|\,Y=\frac{5}{8}) & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{5}{8})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}\frac{2x}{{(\frac{5}{8})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{64}{25}{\int }_{1/4}^{1/2}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{64}{25}[{x}^{2}]_{1/4}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{64}{25}(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{64}{25}(\frac{3}{16}) \\  & =\frac{12}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}24xy, & \,0<x<1,0<y<1-x \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Find $P(Y<X\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

Using the formula for the marginal density function for $X,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1-x}24xy\,\text{d}y \\  & =24x{\int }_{0}^{1-x}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =24x{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1-x} \\  & =12x(1-x)^{2}-0 \\  & =12x(x-1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}12x(x-1)^{2}, & \,0<x<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)}.
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal density function for $X.$

Now, for $0<x<1,0<y<1-x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{24xy}{12x(x-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2y}{(x-1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{(x-1)^{2}}, & \,0<x<1,0<y<1-x \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute our probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<X\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}) & =P(Y<\frac{1}{3}\,|\,X=\frac{1}{3}) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\frac{1}{3})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}\frac{2y}{{(\frac{1}{3}-1)}^{2}}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1/3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}(\frac{1}{18}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2y}{2x+3} & \,0\le x\le 1,\,x+1\le y\le x+2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y<2\,|\,X=\frac{3}{4}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(Y\in A\,|\,X=x)={\int }_{A}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x)$ is the conditional probability density function of $Y$ given $X=x.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<2\,|\,X=\frac{3}{4}) & ={\int }_{1+x}^{2}{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,x=\frac{3}{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1+3/4}^{2}\frac{2y}{(2\cdot \frac{3}{4}+3)}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{\int }_{7/4}^{2}2y\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}[{y}^{2}]_{7/4}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(4-\frac{49}{16}) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}6, & \,y\le x\le \sqrt{y},\,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $y\le x\le \sqrt{y},\,0<y<1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{y}^{\sqrt{y}}6\,\text{d}x \\  & =6\cdot x\,{|}_{y}^{\sqrt{y}} \\  & =6(\sqrt{y}-y).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}6(\sqrt{y}-y), & \,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $y\le x\le \sqrt{y},\,0<y<1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{6}{6(\sqrt{y}-y)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}-y}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}-y}, & \,y\le x\le \sqrt{y},\,0<y<1, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following joint probability density function:

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}({y}^{2}+x), & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the expression of the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ for $0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the marginal density function for $Y,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{8}({y}^{2}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{8}+\frac{3x}{8})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{8}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{16}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{6{y}^{2}}{8}+\frac{12}{16}-0 \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{2}}{4}+\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}({y}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the following:

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}({y}^{2}+1), & \,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Now recall that the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ for two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)},
$$

where

- $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability density function for $X$ and $Y,$ and

- ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal density function for $Y.$

Now, for $1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{8}({y}^{2}+x))}{(\frac{3}{4}({y}^{2}+1))} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}+x}{2({y}^{2}+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

For other values of $x$ and $y,$ the function $f(x,y)$ equals $0.$ As a result, ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ will be equal to $0$ too.

Therefore, the conditional probability density function is the following:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}+x}{2({y}^{2}+1)}, & \,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
